findings.title: confine.py exec-neutering misses the underlying spawn primitive
findings.desc: The new `_no_exec` patches `os.*` exec names and the public `subprocess` wrappers, but not `_posixsubprocess.fork_exec` — the primitive `subprocess` itself calls, reachable as a module attribute (e.g. `import pathlib; pathlib.sys.modules['subprocess']._posixsubprocess`, since confine.py's own imports populate `sys.modules` and none of `.sys`/`.modules`/`._posixsubprocess`/`.fork_exec` are gate-blocked). An exec'd child runs entirely outside confine.py's in-process monkey-patches, so on the `unshare -rn` tier (shared mount namespace, no loud warning) the filesystem-write boundary collapses; `os.kill`/`os.killpg` also remain usable for host-process DoS. The new comment "neuter subprocess even if reached by reflection" and decision 019's "confine.py neuters … process execution" overstate what this layer delivers.

findings.title: bwrap run fails when CWD is under /tmp, and probe can't catch it
findings.desc: The real invocation now uses `--chdir "$PWD"`, but the fresh `--tmpfs /tmp` shadows any working directory under /tmp, so bwrap dies on chdir — while the probe (which omits `--chdir` and the `$AE` bind) still succeeds, and since only the probe sits in the `if` condition there is no degradation to the fallback tier; Mode 2 just errors out. Previously `--chdir /tmp` always worked, so this is a regression for projects living under /tmp; the probe should mirror the real argv (including `--chdir "$PWD"`) or a failed run should fall through to the unshare tier.

findings.title: "confine.py neuters network egress" overstates the socket patch
findings.desc: The socket hooks cover `connect`/`connect_ex`/`create_connection`/`getaddrinfo` but not UDP `sendto`/`sendmsg`, which need neither connect nor DNS resolution (literal-IP datagrams), so egress is still possible on the no-sandbox fallback tier. The tier is admittedly best-effort and carries a warning, but the categorical "neuters … network egress" claim (and the "network disabled" error text) should be qualified.

findings.title: stale "write methods are blocked below" comment
findings.desc: With the `open()` mode gate removed in this diff, nothing "below" in check.py blocks pathlib write methods anymore — containment is runtime-only. The comment "pathlib is approved for READS; its write methods are blocked below and at runtime" should drop "below".

findings.title: "Prefer absolute paths" rationale doesn't follow
findings.desc: Relative reads now resolve against the caller's real working directory on every tier (bwrap does `--chdir "$PWD"`), so absolute-vs-relative changes nothing for read success; the claim that a moved data file "will fail cleanly rather than silently" only with absolute paths is muddled and will confuse users about what actually changed.

findings.title: Process confinement is trivially bypassable outside bwrap
findings.desc: Removing `.system` from the static denylist while only monkeypatching `os`/`subprocess` permits code such as `numpy.ctypeslib.ctypes.CDLL(None).system(...)`. On the advertised `unshare -rn` tier this executes arbitrary commands against the host mount namespace without any warning, contradicting the claim that runtime confinement blocks process execution.

findings.title: Dynamic positional allow_pickle bypasses the gate
findings.desc: The new check rejects the third `np.load` argument only when it is a truthy `ast.Constant`; `flag=True; np.load(path, None, flag)` or `np.load(path, None, bool(1))` passes and enables pickle deserialization. Non-literal values must fail closed unless they are provably false.

findings.title: Newly permitted open writes can modify shared host temp files
findings.desc: After removing the static `open()` mode restriction, `confine.py` accepts writes anywhere under `tempfile.gettempdir()`—normally all of `/tmp`—rather than only the invocation's `$AE` scratch directory. An accepted script can therefore truncate or create host-visible temp files, contrary to the stated “outside scratch” protection.

findings.title: bwrap fails for working directories beneath /tmp
findings.desc: The real sandbox overlays `/tmp` with a private tmpfs and then changes directory to `$PWD`, but only `$AE` is rebound into that tmpfs. If the checkout/caller directory is under `/tmp`, the probe succeeds while the real invocation fails at `--chdir` instead of degrading to another tier.

findings.title: Non-literal positional `allow_pickle` bypasses the deserialization gate
findings.desc: The new check rejects only a truthy `ast.Constant`, so `flag = True; np.load(path, None, flag)` passes and executes a malicious pickle. On the `unshare`/fallback tiers this yields arbitrary Python before the best-effort hooks can provide a sound host boundary, enabling host code execution via native/reflection paths.

findings.title: Write-mode `open()` is not contained for repositories under `/tmp`
findings.desc: Removing the static mode check relies on `confine.py`, but that helper treats all of `tempfile.gettempdir()`—normally `/tmp`—as writable. On non-bwrap tiers, a working tree under `/tmp` can therefore be modified directly with `open(..., "w")`, contrary to the stated outside-scratch protection.

findings.title: bwrap execution fails when the working directory is under `/tmp`
findings.desc: The private `--tmpfs /tmp` hides the caller’s working directory, yet the real invocation now uses `--chdir "$PWD"` without rebinding that directory. The probe does not test this `--chdir`, so it succeeds and selects bwrap, after which the actual run fails instead of degrading to another tier.

findings.title: bwrap tier does not block newly allowed process creation
findings.desc: Removing `system`/`fork`/`spawn*` from the gate makes process creation readily reachable through approved-module references such as pandas’ exposed `os`, while only `confine.py` patches those functions; the bwrap branch does not. Its namespaces and per-process limits do not impose a process-count limit, leaving straightforward fork/process-exhaustion DoS despite the documentation claiming process execution is enforced at runtime.

findings.title: `allow_pickle` positional-arg check now misses variable/expression arguments
findings.desc: The `np.load(...)` 3rd-positional-arg guard was changed from "reject any 3-arg call" to "reject only if the 3rd arg is a literal Constant that is truthy," so `np.load(f, mode, some_var)` where `some_var` evaluates truthy at runtime now passes the static gate undetected, weakening the deserialization-RCE guard beyond what the accompanying comment/doc implies ("truthy 3rd positional arg" is checked, but non-literal truthy args are silently allowed through).

findings.title: bwrap probe does not mirror the real invocation's flags
findings.desc: The comment claims the probe uses "the SAME mounts the real run uses" so a policy-denied host degrades gracefully, but the probe omits `--ro-bind "$AE" "$AE"`, `--chdir`, `--new-session`, and `--clearenv $ENV` that the real run adds. If any of these additional flags fail on a given host (e.g. seccomp/AppArmor denying `--new-session` or `--clearenv`), the probe will pass but the real bwrap invocation will fail outright with no fallback to the `unshare`/resource-limit tiers, contradicting the stated degrade-not-fail design goal.

findings.title: Matplotlib cache comment inaccurate for the bwrap tier
findings.desc: `MPL="$AE/mpl"` is introduced with the comment "matplotlib cache under $AE → cleaned by the trap," but the bwrap `ENV` string still hardcodes `--setenv MPLCONFIGDIR /tmp/mpl` (unchanged by this diff), so under the bwrap tier the cache actually goes to the tmpfs `/tmp/mpl`, not `$AE/mpl`. The comment is only accurate for the non-bwrap tiers, creating a misleading description of the bwrap code path.

findings.title: allow_pickle positional-arg check narrowed to literal-only, unlike the keyword form
findings.desc: The rewritten `check.py` only rejects `np.load(file, mode, X)` when the 3rd positional arg is a literal truthy constant (`isinstance(node.args[2], ast.Constant) and bool(node.args[2].value)`), whereas the adjacent `allow_pickle=` keyword check still fails closed on any non-provably-`False` value. A computed/variable 3rd positional argument (e.g. `np.load(f, None, some_expr)`) now silently passes the static gate even though it can enable pickle-deserialization RCE, an inconsistency with the "fail closed on unprovable" philosophy applied everywhere else in the same file.

findings.title: bwrap `--chdir "$PWD"` can be shadowed by the fresh `--tmpfs /tmp` mount
findings.desc: The diff switches bwrap's working directory from a fixed `/tmp` to the caller's `$PWD`, and the surrounding comment/doc claims "CWD stays the caller's dir (read-only) so relative data reads work." However, `--tmpfs /tmp` is mounted before the (only) explicit re-bind of `$AE`; if the caller's `$PWD` happens to live under `/tmp` (a common location for scratch/CI working dirs), it will be shadowed by the empty tmpfs rather than the real read-only directory, silently breaking relative-path data reads instead of the "fail cleanly" behavior the doc promises.

findings.title: `$AE/mpl` cache dir is unused under the bwrap tier
findings.desc: `MPL="$AE/mpl"` is created and exported via `MPLCONFIGDIR="$MPL"`, but the bwrap `$ENV` string still hardcodes `--setenv MPLCONFIGDIR /tmp/mpl`, a different path inside the sandbox's fresh tmpfs. The mkdir'd `$AE/mpl` (bound read-only under `$AE`) is therefore never actually used on the bwrap tier — harmless in practice (matplotlib creates `/tmp/mpl` itself) but a leftover inconsistency from the relocation.
